# Volume 3 — Chapter XXI Roses of Yesterday

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The two weeks that Nell passed in Harborough were extremely enjoyable, though a subtle undertone of obscure ache and discontent coursed through the period whenever Hugh crossed her mind. Still, she had few opportunities to ponder over him. A most lively spot was "Mount Holly," the lovely, historic Lindsay family estate, which swarmed with Cressy’s male and female companions. A almost dizzying sequence of excursions, balls, outings, and rowing gatherings occurred—every one of which Cressy vividly grouped together as "jamborees"; Hector and Orlando were present so incessantly that Nell pondered whether their sole occupation was catering to the whims of that elusive Cressy. Each was a pleasant, honorable young man, yet Nell refused to be persuaded to judge which of the two was preferable.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0000 }

“And I was relying so heavily on you to assist me in deciding which one I ought to give my pledge of marriage to,” lamented Cressy.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0001 }

“That is something you have to accomplish on your own. Deciding which spouses are suitable for everyone else is a skill you have truly mastered,” Nell replied, with a somewhat biting tone.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0002 }

“Ah, that is a completely distinct matter,” Cressy stated, in truth.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0003 }

Yet the most delightful moment of Nell’s stay in Harborough occurred when she visited where she was born—that small, faded yellow dwelling on a secluded street which had so frequently filled her dreams. Her eyes shone with joy as she gazed upon it, stepping through the gate alongside Cressy.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0004 }

“It matches my mental image nearly to a tee,” she remarked. “Although honeysuckle does not drape over the windows, a lilac tree stands near the gate, and—indeed, muslin curtains hang in the windows. It brings me such joy that the yellow paint remains.”
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0005 }

The door was opened by a woman who was extremely thin and extremely tall.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0006 }

“Indeed, two decades back, the Shirleys were residents here,” she remarked, responding to the query from Nell. “The place was leased by them. My memory holds them. Fever claimed both of their lives at the same time. A deeply tragic event occurred. A baby was left behind by them. My assumption is that it passed away a long time back. That child was frail. The child was taken in by Old Thomas and his spouse—just as though they lacked a sufficient number of their own children.”
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0007 }

“It failed to perish,” Nell remarked, grinning, “and I was the infant in question.”
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0008 }

“Is that so! Well, you have gotten bigger,” the woman cried out, appearing greatly astonished that Nell was no longer an infant. “Now that I examine you, I notice the likeness. Your complexion is like your pa’s. Red hair was what he had. However, your eyes and mouth look like your ma’s. A sweet little person was what she was. Her school was attended by my darter, who was almost wild about her. A single grave held both of them when they were buried, and a tombstone was erected for them by the School Board as a recompense for devoted service. Will you step inside?”
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0009 }

“May I be allowed to explore the entire house?” Nell asked with enthusiasm.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0010 }

“Goodness, certainly, go right ahead if that is your wish. It will be quick—since the place is quite small. My husband gets no peace from me about constructing another kitchen, yet moving fast is not his way. That door leads to the parlor, while a pair of rooms sits on the upper floor. Feel free to wander around on your own. My attention is needed by the baby. Your birth took place in the room facing east. Your mother expressing her fondness for watching the dawn comes back to me; moreover, I recall being told that your arrival occurred exactly as the sun ascended, making its beams upon your countenance the initial sight your mother beheld.”
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0011 }

Nell climbed the tight staircase and stepped into that small east room with her heart overflowing. To her, it resembled a sanctuary. In this place, her mother had envisioned the lovely, joyful visions of awaiting motherhood; in this place, that crimson dawn illumination had washed over the two of them during the holy moment of delivery; in this place, her mother had passed away. Nell gazed around herself with awe, her eyes filled with tears. For her, it represented one of life’s precious moments that shine brilliantly always in recollection.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0012 }

“Only consider that—when I came into the world, mother was not as old as I currently am,” she murmured.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0013 }

As Nell descended the stairs, the mistress of the home encountered her in the hallway. A small, dusty bundle secured with a washed-out blue ribbon was extended toward her by the woman.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0014 }

“In this upstairs closet, I stumbled upon a package of ancient mail after I moved in,” she remarked. “Their contents are unknown to me—as I did not care to examine them, yet ‘Miss Bertha Willis’ is written on the first one, which happened to be your mother's unmarried name. Should you desire to possess them, they are yours to keep.”
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0015 }

“Oh, thank you—thank you,” Nell cried, clutching the bundle with delight.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0016 }

“That was everything the house contained,” her hostess stated. “The doctor bills were paid by selling all the furniture, and your ma’s clothes and small possessions were given to Mrs. Thomas. I suppose those things did not last very long with such a crowd of Thomas children. If I remember them correctly, they were destructive young animals.”
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0017 }

“There is not a single item of my mother's in my possession,” Nell said, her voice filled with emotion. “I—I will never be able to offer you sufficient thanks for these letters.”
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0018 }

“I am happy to do it. Goodness, your eyes really resemble your mother's. Hers were capable of practically speaking. Your dad was rather plain-looking, yet extremely pleasant. When their wedding took place, I remember people remarking that a couple had never been so deeply devoted to one another—Poor things, their lives ended not long after; nevertheless, their time together was filled with tremendous happiness, which I reckon is worth a lot.”
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0019 }

Nell yearned to return home so that she might read her cherished correspondence, yet she undertook a brief journey prior to doing so. Solitarily, she visited the verdant section of the “old” Harborough cemetery where her father and mother lay buried, depositing the white blossoms she brought with her upon their grave. Subsequently, she hurried back to Mount Holly, sequestered herself within her chamber, and perused the letters. A portion had been penned by her father, and others by her mother. They were few in quantity—totaling merely twelve—because Edmund and Bertha Harcourt had rarely been apart throughout their courtship. Aged, discolored, and faint, the correspondence was smudged by the passage of time. No deep expressions of intellect were written upon the discolored and creased sheets, which contained solely messages of affection and faith. The charm of bygone moments adhered to them—the distant, affectionate dreams of those lovers who had died long ago. Bertha Harcourt had been endowed with the talent for composing letters that captured the author's delightful character in phrasing and ideas that kept their grace and sweetness across the years. These writings were gentle, private, and hallowed. For Nell, the most delightful among them was the note composed following her arrival into the world and sent to her father during a short trip away. It was packed with a glowing, youthful mother’s descriptions of “baby”—her intelligence, her brilliance, and her innumerable charming traits.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0020 }

“When she is sleeping, I love her most, and even more when she is awake,” was what Bertha Harcourt had set down in the postscript. It was likely the final line she had ever written. Her end was extremely close.
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0021 }

“This day has been more beautiful to me than any other,” Nell told Cressy later that evening. “My father and mother have been FOUND by me. They have been made REAL to me by those letters. I am no longer an orphan. It feels to me as though I opened a book and discovered sweet, beloved roses of yesterday pressed between its pages.”
{: #nw-v03-c21-p0022 }
